sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**

Larsen & Toubro (LT) is a diversified conglomerate with a presence in multiple sectors, including infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, and services. The company's operating segments are identified based on business activities, revenue generation, and expense incurrence, with four reportable segments: Infrastructure Projects, Energy Projects, Hi-Tech Manufacturing, and Others. As of March 31, 2025, LT's non-current assets stood at ₹17,742.53 crore, with ₹17,387.28 crore attributed to Indian operations and ₹355.25 crore to foreign countries. The company's revenue streams are diversified, with no single customer contributing more than 10% of total revenue.

**Investment Thesis**

Our investment thesis for LT is centered on the company's diversified business portfolio, strong execution capabilities, and growth potential in key sectors. With a robust balance sheet and a proven track record of delivering complex projects, LT is well-positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities in infrastructure, energy, and manufacturing. The company's focus on technology and innovation, as evident in its Hi-Tech Manufacturing segment, is expected to drive growth and profitability in the long term. While the current financial data is limited, LT's segment reporting and accounting policies provide a transparent view of its operations, allowing investors to make informed decisions. Overall, we believe that LT's diversified business model, strong execution capabilities, and growth potential make it an attractive investment opportunity for long-term investors.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: L&T operates across multiple business segments, including Infrastructure Projects, Energy Projects, Hi-Tech Manufacturing, IT & Technology Services, Financial Services, Development Projects, and Others. For the year ended March 31, 2025, the company reported a consolidated total revenue of ₹142,509.01 crore, with segment revenue as per Ind AS 115 being ₹141,532.97 crore. The segment-wise revenue breakdown is as follows: Infrastructure Projects (₹103,742.51 crore), Energy Projects (₹23,934.45 crore), Hi-Tech Manufacturing (₹9,797.02 crore), and Others (₹4,058.99 crore). The Hi-Tech Manufacturing segment achieved order inflows of ₹18,282 crore during FY 2024-25, registering growth of 28.0% over the previous year. The segment's revenue for the year was ₹10,181 crore, registering a growth of 16.1% y-o-y. The company's consolidated profit after tax (PAT) for FY 2024-25 was ₹15,037 crore, increasing by 15.1% over the previous year. The Return on Net Worth (RONW) for FY 2024-25 was higher at 16.3%, compared to 14.9% in the previous year, mainly on account of higher profitability.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The company's financial performance is highlighted by its revenue and net profit growth. As per the consolidated financials, the gross revenue from operations for FY25 was ₹255,734 crore, and the profit for the year was ₹17,673 crore. In comparison, the gross revenue from operations for FY24 was ₹221,113 crore, with a profit for the year of ₹15,547 crore. The profit after tax (PAT) for FY25, including exceptional items, was ₹15,037 crore, representing a 15.1% increase over the previous year's PAT of ₹13,059 crore.

The company's Return on Net Worth (RONW) for FY25 was 16.3%, higher than the 14.9% recorded in the previous year, primarily due to improved profitability. The net worth attributable to the owners of the company as of March 31, 2025, was ₹97,656 crore, reflecting a net increase of ₹11,297 crore compared to the position as of March 31, 2024.

sections.body:

The company's approach to accounting for foreign currency transactions, including translating assets and liabilities at the closing rate and income and expenses at the average exchange rate, follows standard practices. The recognition of exchange differences in other comprehensive income and their accumulation in equity as a foreign currency translation reserve indicates a methodical approach to handling currency risks. While specific details on the company's cash flow, such as operating cash flow, investing cash flow, and financing cash flow, are not provided, the company's management of foreign exchange risks and its accounting policies suggest a structured approach to financial management. sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of LTTS has outlined a robust risk management framework, strategically aligned with the company's business strategy and embedded in its normal course of business. This framework includes four risk categories: Strategic, Operational, Financial, and Compliance. The company conducts risk assessments at various levels, including enterprise, business unit, customer account, and project levels, and presents key risks to senior management, including the CEO, CFO, and relevant Board Committees. As of March 31, 2025, the company's non-current assets stood at ₹17,742.53 crore, with ₹17,387.28 crore attributed to India and ₹355.25 crore to foreign countries.

Looking ahead, the management is optimistic about the company's growth trajectory, driven by its expertise in engineering and digital innovation. With investments in high-potential areas like Agentic AI, LTTS is well-positioned to lead the global ER&D market. The company's focus on key growth segments, including mobility, sustainability, and tech, is expected to drive growth, powered by its 'Go Deeper to Scale' strategy. The acquisition of Intelliswift Inc and its subsidiaries in Q3 FY 2024-25 has strengthened the company's foothold in hyperscaler segments and marked its entry into service-led sectors like retail, fintech, and healthcare. As of 2024-25, the company's revenue from operations stood at ₹255,734.45 crore, with ₹128,168.58 crore generated from India and ₹127,565.87 crore from foreign countries. The management remains committed to client-centric innovation and engineering excellence, fostering technology-driven transformation across industries worldwide.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with LTTS are primarily related to its operational, financial, and strategic aspects. From a financial risk perspective, the company is exposed to foreign exchange rate and interest rate risks, which may adversely affect its revenues, cost, and profitability. As of the latest reporting period, the company has both receivable and payable exposures in foreign currency, and changes in exchange rates may necessitate adjustments to local currency product pricing due to competitive pressures. To mitigate these risks, the company enters into foreign currency forward and option contracts with financial institutions. Additionally, the company's practice is to hedge a portion of its material net foreign exchange exposures with tenors in line with the project/business life cycle.

The company's risk management framework also identifies strategic, operational, and compliance risks as key areas of concern. Strategic risks may hinder the company's ability to achieve its objectives and goals, while operational challenges may impact its regular business activities. Compliance risks, on the other hand, relate to the potential non-compliance with laws and regulations. The company's risk management programme is designed to proactively identify and mitigate these enterprise risks, supporting informed decision-making, sustainable growth, and value creation. However, the effectiveness of this programme in managing key risks is subject to various factors, including the company's ability to accurately estimate costs and revenues, particularly in relation to construction contracts, where significant accounting judgements are involved. The company's auditor has identified revenue recognition as a key audit matter, highlighting the significance of estimating revenue and costs to complete contracts with customers.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
The company has witnessed significant developments in its recent past, particularly in terms of geographical revenue distribution and research and development expenditures. As of the financial year 2024-25, the company's revenue from India stood at ₹128,168.58 crore, while revenue from foreign countries amounted to ₹127,565.87 crore, with notable contributions from the United States of America (₹33,448.58 crore), the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (₹61,002.04 crore), and the United Arab Emirates (₹9,469.87 crore). The total revenue for the year was ₹255,734.45 crore. In terms of non-current assets, the company held ₹50,796.87 crore in India and ₹3,088.65 crore in foreign countries as of March 31, 2025.

The company has also been actively engaged in research and development activities, with recognized expenses of ₹171.86 crore in the financial year 2024-25, along with capital expenditures on tangible assets (₹2.40 crore) and other intangible assets (₹0.77 crore). Furthermore, the company has been managing its foreign exchange rate and interest rate risks through regular reviews of its exposures and the use of hedge contracts, including foreign currency forward and option contracts, to protect against potential losses. However, the company's risk management practices and potential impact on its financial condition and operating results warrant continued monitoring.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The 'Bull vs Bear vs Base Case' scenario for LTTS is shaped by its strategic positioning, risk management framework, and growth prospects. On the bull case, LTTS's proven expertise in engineering and digital innovation, combined with its investments in high-potential areas such as Agentic AI, positions the company for a robust growth trajectory. The acquisition of Intelliswift Inc and its subsidiaries in Q3 FY 2024-25 is expected to strengthen its foothold in hyperscaler segments and expand its software and digital engineering capabilities, potentially driving revenue growth. With a research and development expenditure of ₹171.86 crore in 2024-25, the company is well-placed to capitalize on emerging opportunities in digital transformation, sustainability, and innovation.

On the bear case, LTTS faces risks associated with foreign exchange rate fluctuations, interest rate risks, and potential non-compliance with laws and regulations. The company's foreign exchange rate risk, with both receivable and payable exposures in foreign currency, may adversely affect revenues, cost, and profitability. Additionally, the company's ability to effectively manage its risk management programme, including identification and mitigation of enterprise risks, will be crucial in navigating potential challenges. The base case scenario assumes that LTTS will continue to leverage its expertise and investments to drive growth, while effectively managing its risk exposures, resulting in a steady growth trajectory. With a strong focus on client-centric innovation and engineering excellence, LTTS is poised to capitalize on emerging opportunities, but the company's ability to execute on its strategy and navigate potential risks will be key to its success.

Key Audit Matters Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgment, were of most significance in our audit of the standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. These matters were addressed in the context of our audit of the standalone financial statements as a whole, and in forming our opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters. We have determined the matters described below to be the key audit matters to be communicated in our report. Revenue recognition – accounting for construction contracts Key audit matter Description There are significant accounting judgements in estimating revenue to be recognised on contracts with customers, including estimation of costs to complete. The Company recognises revenue on the basis of stage of completion in proportion of the contract costs incurred at balance sheet date, relative to the total estimated costs of the contract at completion. The recognition of revenue is therefore dependent on estimates in relation to total estimated costs of each such contract. Significant judgements are involved in determining the expected losses, when such losses become probable based on the expected total contract cost. Cost contingencies are included in these estimates to take into account specific risks of uncertainties or disputed claims against the Company, arising within each contract. These contingencies are reviewed by the Company’s Management on a regular basis throughout the life of the contract and adjusted where appropriate. The revenue on contracts may also include variable consideration (change orders and claims). Variable consideration is recognised when the recovery of such consideration is highly probable based on company’s contractual rights and /or a legal assessment.

The Company primarily follows cash flow hedge accounting for Highly Probable Forecasted Exposures (HPFE), hence, the movement in mark to market (MTM) of the hedge contracts undertaken for such exposures is likely to be offset by contra movements in the underlying exposures values. However, till the point of time that the HPFE becomes an on-balance sheet exposure, the changes in MTM of the hedge contracts will impact the Balance Sheet of the Company. Further, given the effective horizons of the Company’s risk management activities which coincide with the durations of the projects under execution, which could extend across 3-4 years and given the business uncertainties associated with the timing and estimation of the project exposures, the recognition of the gains and losses related to these instruments may not always coincide with the timing of gains and losses related to the underlying economic exposures and, therefore, may affect the Company’s financial condition and operating results. The Company monitors the potential risk arising out of the market factors like exchange rates, interest rates, price of traded investment products etc. on a regular basis. For on-balance Sheet exposures, the Company monitors the risks on net unhedged exposures. (i) Foreign exchange rate risk: The Company has both receivable and payable exposures in foreign currency. Accordingly, changes in exchange rates may adversely affect the Company’s revenues, cost, and profitability. There is a risk that the Company may also have to adjust the local currency product pricing due to competitive pressures when there has been significant volatility in foreign currency exchange rates. The Company may enter foreign currency forward and option contracts with financial institutions to protect against foreign exchange risks associated with existing assets and liabilities, firm commitments, forecasted future cash flows and net investments in foreign subsidiaries. In addition, the Company has entered, and may enter in future, into non-designated foreign currency contracts to partially offset the foreign currency exchange gains and losses on its foreign-denominated debt issuances. The Company’s practice is to hedge a portion of its material net foreign exchange exposures with tenors in line with the project/business life cycle. The Company may also choose not to hedge certain foreign exchange exposures.

Risk Management Framework The company’s risk management approach is strategically placed to function independently in line with best-in- class corporate governance principles and statutory requirements in alignment with globally accepted risk management frameworks. LTTS’s risk management programme is aligned with business strategy and embedded in the normal course of business across the company under the guidance of the Risk Management Committee (RMC) of the Board. The programme enables proactive identification and mitigation of enterprise risks, supporting informed decision-making, sustainable growth and value creation. The Chief Risk Officer oversees risk management programme and is supported by the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team. LTTS’s risk management framework includes the following risk categories: à Strategic: Risk events that make it difficult to achieve strategic objectives and goals à Operational: Operational challenges faced by business teams in regular course of business à Financial: Inefficient utilisation of financial resources, currency fluctuations, credit risk, etc. à Compliance: Potential risk of non-compliance with laws and regulations For the effective functioning of the risk management programme, risk assessments are conducted at various levels, including enterprise, business unit, customer account and project levels. Key risks are presented to the senior management including the CEO, the CFO and the relevant Board Committees such as Audit Committee and Risk Management Committee. Outlook LTTS continues to leverage its proven expertise in engineering and digital innovation for driving a robust growth trajectory in the coming year. With ongoing investments in high-potential areas including Agentic AI, LTTS is well-positioned to lead the global ER&D market. The focus continues to remain on key growth segments of mobility, sustainability and tech, powered by its ‘Go Deeper to Scale’ strategy and the momentum generated by the accelerated emergence of breakthrough technologies. LTTS’s acquisition of Intelliswift Inc and its subsidiaries in Q3 FY 2024-25 underscores its commitment to expanding software and digital engineering capabilities. The move not only strengthens its foothold in hyperscaler segments but also marks its entry into service-led sectors such as retail, fintech and healthcare. The integration of this acquisition has already shown results with the creation of a new Software & Platforms segment designed to address the growing demand for innovative software solutions. With the continued growth in demand for digital transformation initiatives, combined with a growing focus on sustainability and innovation, LTTS is well poised to capitalise on emerging opportunities. Aligned with its commitment towards client-centric innovation and engineering excellence, the company continues to foster technology- driven transformation across industries worldwide.
